title: Establish whether GP8 can preserve explicit empty beats
scope: Determine whether an authored empty beat can remain distinct from a rest in GP8 and in the pinned consumer.
acceptance: Compare an empty voice slot, an explicit empty beat and a note-free rest using independent wire inspection.
Identify any supported target encoding that preserves the public BeatStatus distinction.
Preserve the distinction if possible; otherwise retain its narrow normalization and strict-policy evidence as an accepted target limit.

reproduction.instructions: Compare an empty voice slot, an explicit empty beat and a note-free rest using independent wire inspection.

evidence.detail: Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
Existing scoped evidence; not proof of all AlphaTab variants.
target-limit: The target cannot distinguish an authored empty timed beat from a rest inside a populated voice. Whole-empty-voice encoding is a different scope.

Compare an absent whole voice, an explicit empty timed beat inside a populated voice, and an ordinary rest. Assert exact voice references and beat wire forms rather than relying only on finalized consumer objects. Verify the explicit-empty-to-rest normalization and strict rejection without losing timing or annotations. Do not use a fake note or remove a timed beat. Resolve the mixed-voice distinction as a target limit once tested. Encoding an entirely empty voice as -1 is separate scope and must not be reported as solving an empty beat inside a populated voice.
